An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into three segments, and discovered that this anisotropy becomes increasingly pronounced with rising energy levels above 4 EeV, exhibiting an energy-dependent pattern that adheres to a power law with an index of 0.79 ± 0.19. We also discovered that the orientation of these anisotropy patterns supports their extragalactic origins, across all energy levels examined. Furthermore, an investigation of quadrupolar components revealed that they lacked sufficient statistical significance. We interpret our findings within the context of theoretical models proposing the distribution of extremely energetic cosmic sources and cosmic magnetic field dynamics.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude are evident in midrapidity mid-transverse-momentum particles. Notably, these fluctuations increase with the level of centrality of the collisions and decrease as $n$ increases. When analyzed using a specific formula, it was discovered that non-linear components of flow, such as trigonometric components and secondary populations of particles, account for a substantial portion of the observed variations. These fluctuations offer valuable information about initial differences in spatial geometry, which can be used to better understand the creation of quark-gluon plasma. They also provide validation for simulations based on hydrodynamic models. Importantly, these findings represent an expansion of knowledge about Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC and improve upon previous studies conducted in lighter particle collisions.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explore theories for handling instances that breach certain dependencies, with no preconditions on the presence of missing values. We establish a framework where each data entry can be associated with a truth status: true, false, inconsistent, or undetermined. Furthermore, our framework facilitates examination of pressing problems like data quality assessment, query validation, and data fusion. Specifically, we investigate the complexity of these problems when queries and relationships are expressed using first-order logic. Our key findings reveal that verifying the consistency of a table is an intractable issue, while other problems involve ranking data rows based their probability of being accurate. Interestingly, this probabilistic aspect allows us to address query validation and data fusion as special cases of those problems.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within such data sets. Furthermore, we have analyzed the theoretical characteristics of the TV-PARX model, demonstrated its superiority over constant parameter models using simulated data, and successfully applied it to forecast COVID-10 weekly admissions in Italian hospitals.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation
tasks with the use of point-based reinforcement learning and a neural network
converting the NDF for each object to a continuous action. Experimentation
reveals that our method successfully teaches an agent to manipulate multiple
objects from varied perspectives and generalize to unseen object categories.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for two-dimensional cases, we have refined $c$-cycle ratios for $N$ values of 1, 3, and 7, as well as universality ratios for lattice gases and Ising models. Similarly, for three-dimensional cases with $N$ values of 1, 3, and 2 effective components, we have adjusted the Yang-Lee edge singularity positions and improved estimates of critical exponents for the divergence of correlation length and the order parameter.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a sampling algorithm in the "easy" regime of these models.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical scientists, its success relies on the research community and astronomers including the aerosol component in their data analysis and宣传. Although aerosal effects can be extracted from co-epochs images of comparable stars, neglecting to account for them in宣传 can cause errors in data that could be misinterpreted as changes in the stars themselves or their data. Since including aerosal components in analysis and宣传 varies, it introduces risks of introducing bias, statistical deviations, and宣传均的问题。However, including aerosal components in分析 and宣传 can provide more accurate results using new technologies, with the assistance of the astronomical community. Using the Gaia data as an example, it is shown how high-precision photometry from Gaia can precisely determine the ground-level aerosal profiles with the aid of machine learning. As an additional demonstration, a Python tool is introduced to recover the aerosal components from the GAPP data with the aerosal variability over time.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using convolutional networks has gained significant interest. Recent approaches typically tackle this problem in two separate steps: first, they generate object response maps to identify potential object locations, and then they estimate the 5 additional degrees of freedom. This, however, often leads to suboptimal performance due to the accumulation of errors from step one. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel framework called Deep Hierarchical Pose Assessment (DETA), which is built on two key components: projection group regression (PGR) and correspondence learning (CL). Instead of accumulating errors, DETA minimizes their impact by simultaneously addressing pixel-level and landmark correspondences. Our experimental results show that the DETA framework leads to notable improvements in accurately estimating object pose.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
hidden variables in Chandrasekaran (2012) and can jointly estimate multiple
inverse covariance matrices, as shown in Danaher (2013) and Tomasi (2018). The
GGLasso package supports the resolution of diverse formulations and notable
subcases like Graphical Lasso with latent variables, Group, and Fused Graphical Lasso.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and assessed, focusing on deterministic impulses, drifts, and Brownian motions. By utilizing the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion, recent studies found that the methods' accuracy could be evaluated in terms of the impact of the step size on configurational averaging. Results showed that for harmonic oscillators, some methods yield precise configurational averages, potentially leading to better performance in biomolecular simulations, especially when constraints are applied. Furthermore, research found that in an anharmonic trimer model, the biocompatible methods offered the most precise outcomes compared to other integrators at high system temperatures. Additionally, research demonstrated that these methods' efficiency could be significantly improved by employing small time steps of 0.0005 ps in an anharmonic trimer model and folded proteins, enabling large-scale simulations of biomolecules with thousands of degrees of freedom.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinct "bounce" phase where the water around the sphere behaves like an acoustic resonator, leading to the ejection of liquid and vapor from the sphere's poles. By conducting numerical simulations using the WHAM solver, we developed an approach to predict surface seal dynamics, bounce durations, and the conditions necessary for bouncing based on sphere impact velocity, water's surface tension, and sphere buoyancy. Notable aspects of our model include incorporating the effects of vaporization, buoyancy, and nonlinear interactions within the fluid, which have been previously neglected in theoretical studies of surface seal. Not all spheres experience a bounce, with slower impacts resulting in a breakdown of the surface seal, leading to a direct splash, whereas faster impacts overcome buoyancy forces, leading to the formation of an air pocket.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to identify the range of universal symmetries potentially present and found that they must include number-theoretic universality while excluding modular universality. Generalized $\theta$-terms in these EFTs then emerge as diagrammatic representations that capture modular transformations.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A significant number of studies have been conducted under magnetic field conditions to analyze the giant Rabi oscillations phenomenon. However, exhibiting giant Rabi oscillations without an external magnetic field is particularly intriguing from a fundamental perspective. In this research, we investigate massive dark excitons under no external magnetic field and observe enormous Rabi oscillations with a frequency that is 4 times greater than those of previous studies. The study also delves into the influence of tunneling between sites on Rabi oscillations.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group, specifically focusing on a unique feature called a screw axis. By applying Su-Schrieffer-Heeger type hopping deformation to this lattice, we are able to identify and analyze "linear nodes" within this two-dimensional space. These nodes, occurring along a path of symmetry, can be visualized akin to an atomic chain exhibiting metallic behavior. Further examining this model, we are able to explore hopf nodes - isolated, complex knots that emerge at specific points on the lattice. Notably, these hopf nodes are confined to a plane of symmetry and persist under various perturbations that break inversion, time-reversal, and chiral symmetry. In visualizing the evolution of a real-space Hamiltonian, we observe that hopping deformation enables interaction between linear nodes, resulting in their migration across the lattice and transformation into hybridized dirac points.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poisson statistics, anti-bunching effects, and quadrature squeezing. These findings demonstrate that SPCCSs possess abundant non-classical behavior, thereby conferring a quantum advantage for executing various technological tasks.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 non-hydrogen atoms within a monomeric structure.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other imaging techniques, medical history, and endoscopic findings. Acquiring and integrating this extra data is time-consuming and costly. Using just CT scans, this study aims to automatically and accurately identify the boundaries of the esophagus and tumors in clinical settings. To do this, we developed an automatic tumor segmentation method based on a custom neural network architecture called DDAUnet, which builds upon a residual attention unet by incorporating three additional modules to automatically adjust feature extraction according to the complexity of the data. To further refine our model, we also tested the incorporation of dense units and global average pooling. When we evaluated our model using the publicly available MESSER dataset, it achieved the lowest average symmetric surface distance for tumor segmentation at 7.99 mm. To increase our model's robustness, we compared it against other state-of-the-art methods by training it on subsets of the MESSER dataset and testing it on the full dataset, demonstrating its superior generalization capabilities. To make our model more explainable, we analyzed the attention maps it produces to better understand its performance.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: education, health, the news, civic participation, and politics. We outline the available datasets, potential applications, and underlying challenges associated with working around data deficiencies, including uneven data availability, ambiguous grammar rules, and gramerless writing. Moreover, we outline potential models, evaluation metrics, and essential factors to consider when creating novel Mixture-of-Tokens (MoT) datasets or training models that cater to specific MoT scenarios. We conclude the paper by outlining promising avenues for future exploration in this complex and intriguing research field.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values and minimal conductivity, making them suitable for next-generation MOSFET applications. To understand the electronic behavior of Ta$_2$O$_5$, researchers have utilized various methods to determine its structure from first principles in materials science. However, its complex crystal lattice makes this task challenging due to multiple possible arrangements. This study presents several Ta$_2$O$_5$ crystal lattice options, none of which match its expected insulating state according to recent findings. It is suggested that the expected bixbyite structure of Ta$_2$O$_5$ may exist, but verifying this requires further investigation into its properties. In addition, a new approach was introduced to predict Ta$_2$O$_5$'s property fluctuations by using Monte Carlo simulations based on the arrangements of tantalum atoms within its structure.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media influences. However, our analysis introduces a novel concept of "big geographic sort" to fill a knowledge gap. This phenomenon occurs when a substantial portion of a nation's population is accessed through a small, dispersed group of platforms, specifically 68% of American Reddit users are accessed via 20 sub-Reddit groups across 45 states. We integrated spatial information into our approach by applying a geographically weighted regression to investigate the impact of place on online misinformation dissemination. Our findings reveal that the "big geographic sort" phenomenon is a significant driver of online misinformation dissemination, accounting for 19% of the variance in false news sharing behavior. We conclude that addressing the structural effects of the big geographic sort is crucial to mitigating the spread of misinformation.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from the instructor. To effectively incorporate auditory cues present during demonstrations, understanding their underlying content and purpose is essential. This study examines audio input from humans instructing a robot using Sawyer via spoken language by analyzing three key features: speech duration, tone variation, and speech content. Evaluating these features across four dimensions, it was discovered that instructors frequently use the same vocabulary to describe specific task elements despite varying situations such as task types, audio instructions, and errors encountered during demonstrations. However, differences in speech patterns including duration and inflection are present across these conditions, showing that human speech carries significant, potentially valuable information for enhancing robotic learning through demonstration-based methods.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and their corresponding Gaussian representations. A promising approach to address this difficulty is through the study of conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, specifically focusing on the universal sector of the energy-momentum tensor in this context. A key unifying framework consists of Euler-Arnold equations, from which we derive three distinct expressions for complexity using the U(1), SU(1,1), and SU(1,N) groups. A straightforward way to compute these expressions is by reducing the dynamics to a single-point ODE system for a coherent state parameter. Additionally, we can establish direct correlations between the state parameter and physical observables, as well as the theory's N-point correlation functions and central charge. A straightforward relation is found between the complexities derived from U(1) and SU(1,N), resulting in a precise connection between these quantities that depends only on the theory's N and the natural time scale.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python, and highlights the key challenges faced in this endeavor. Specifically, we highlight the difficulties in establishing a precise specification for desired system behavior and comparing the meaning of utterances.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommender systems. In cross-domain settings, a multitude of loosely connected sub-domains is often present, albeit underutilized in current research that predominantly focuses on single high-sparsity domains. To bridge this knowledge gap, we introduce a novel recommendation framework called "Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation" (MSD-CR), which exploits the full potential of multiple domains to enhance performance. Presently, single-domain preference sharing methods struggle with the computational complexity of inter-changing multiple domains. To resolve this challenge, we propose a cutting-edge "Enhanced Comprehensive Aspect Preference Learning" (ECAP) model that extracts salient features from each domain and facilitates mutual learning through a shared aspect space. Furthermore, we integrate a novel multi-domain generative adversarial network (MD-GAN) to strengthen data representation and bridge the heterogeneity of domains. Abundant experiments on real-world datasets validate the superior efficacy of our proposed model.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a wide assortment of predefined exotic cones. It then generates simplified equivalent formulations for various optimization applications that can provide significant improvements in processing speed and memory consumption. The proposed method demonstrates a marked improvement in problem-solving efficiency when compared to more conventional and complex conic formulations.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control methods to identify and remove corrupted scans. This paper tackles the issue of learning MRI quality control generalization problem by incorporating the concept of factor learning. We propose a novel approach that leverages the number of artifacts and learning the combination of present factors in the input data. This method enables models to produce more robust results with improved generalization capabilities. Our proposed model incorporates a set of explicit and implicit factor representations to capture the complexity of data. We evaluate our approach on two distinct datasets and establish a benchmark for quality control. We further explore the utility of factor learning in the context of QC, yielding valuable insights.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

This paper explores the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x=0.25$, $0.50$, $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the framework of density functional theory. Our findings reveal that GdSn3 and CmSn3 adopt a CaAg3Sn3 structure type with space group $F\bar{3}m$. Notably, both materials exhibit half-metallic behavior, and the total magnetization is saturated at 8$\mu_B$ per formula unit for GdSn3 and 7$\mu_B$ per formula unit for CmSn3. Neutron diffraction data indicate that Gd atoms carry the majority of the magnetic moments in these compounds. Total magnetic anisotropy energy is calculated to be -0.00016 meV per formula unit for GdSn3 and -0.00011 meV per formula unit for CmSn3, favoring the easy magnetization along the c-axis in both cases.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the Standard Model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the symmetry of the theory to $SU(2) \times U(1)$ and adding two doublets of $SU(2)$ charged fields. Initially, this model was proposed to give a natural explanation for the dark matter abundance observed in the universe. The procedure to calculate the bilepton, quark, and quark-bileptoned quark predicted abundances is discussed, along with how these abundances compare to the observed dark matter. The effects of bilepton and quark production and annihilation on the cosmic microwave background and on the abundance of hydrogen in the universe are also considered, with corresponding limits being discussed. The procedure to calculate the biological and pile-up quark and bilepton thresholds is discussed, along with how these thresholds compare to those of the Standard Model. The consequences of discovering the bilepton at a particle accelerator are discussed.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends this connection to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by standardizing the ordered generating sequences, which allows us to identify exchange laws and a refinement of the Diophantines property. Notably, the standard version exhibits a straightforward connection to the standard Coxeter presentation, while also demonstrating that all Bn subgroups can be uniquely represented. Moreover, the standard version of the ordered generating sequences for Bn offers a more precise version that applies to the general linear group GL(n+1,F).

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate local matter distribution around each supernova via weak lensing convergence. This approach enables us to determine the lensing potential and mass lensing effect experienced by each SN Ia. By leveraging the relationships between lensing parameters and the distributions of surrounding large-scale structure and ELG brightness, we can derive statistical properties of lensing effects. Our research shows that lensing-induced biases for key parameters result in approximately 10 percent changes in correlation functions and 5 percent shifts in mean values for well-limited bands. Furthermore, lensing introduces a correlation between the lensing effect and the brightness of the observed supernovae, amounting to a 0.15 to 0.25 percent effect on the lensing-induced auto-correlation and cross-correlation. These findings highlight the potential for employing type Ia supernovae in measuring dark energy through the analysis of lensing effects.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, thanks to their unique optical properties in the O-band region and long-lived electronic and nuclear spin lifetimes. Although research on these defect centers has so far been conducted as part of bulk silicon studies, we demonstrate the consistent creation of high T center densities within the 220nm device layer of Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) wafers, using a process that combines ion implantation and heat treatment. By developing a method to measure spin-dependent optical transitions, we found that high T center densities located near the interface can exhibit ~1 GHz levels of spectral diffusion without the need for extensive optimization of the fabrication process.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context for recognition in varying ways.
This study categorizes object detectors into 3 groups based on context usage:
one that doesn't use context by isolating the input, another that uses partial
context by isolating part of the feature map, and one that uses full context
without isolation.
Our evaluation method assesses the effect of context for each deep detector
category systematically. A specially designed dataset is created to test the
effect of context for deep detectors. The effect of removing the background
context and foreground objects on the MS COCO is also examined.
It is shown that both two-stage and single-stage object detectors can make use
of the context due to their extensive receptive field.
Thus, selecting the most suitable object detector should depend on the specific
context in question.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon h_i(x)$ holds for $i=1,\ldots,k$ in the domain $\Omega$, where $\beta$ is a non-negative value, $f_i$ exhibits singular growth near the origin with respect to the variable $x$ and satisfies some other conditions, $h_i$ belongs to a specific function space, $\varepsilon$ is a non-negative value, $k$ is a positive integer, and the norm $\|\cdot\|$ represents the Sobolev norm. By making use of the truncation technique, the mountain pass and the nonlinear fountain theorems, we derive several multiplicity results for the given system of equations.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube. These vectors must adhere to either the stochastic covering property or the strong Rayleigh property. Our findings provide improvements over previously established bounds derived by Boucheron, Lugosi, and Massart in Theorem 2.9 and 3.1 of their 2013 book. Specifically, when assessing functions under the stochastic covering property, we obtain comparable bounds to those established under the log-concave measure property. However, when assessing functions under the strong Rayleigh property, we achieve significant enhancements, particularly in the context of polynomial functions under the independent setting.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques were developed to overcome the immunological difficulties. Patients receiving incompatible transplants face a higher risk of transplant rejection, infection, and cancer, and are more likely to lose their transplants. We aim to find the optimal acceptance criteria for end-stage kidney patients by applying modern math and operational research techniques, considering limited time for immunosuppressive therapy, long-term consequences of such therapy, and the possibility of organ loss. Additionally, we consider supply competition among patients,有限的 supply necessitates careful allocation resources. Our model yields insights into treatment duration, acceptance standards, desensitization techniques, and kidney allocation, which were validated using data from the United States Transplant and Renal Disease registries, specifically the UNET dataset.

This paper conducts a comparative analysis of the Loughran-McDonald financial emotions vocabulary and the UNLEx financial emotions vocabulary, focusing on their embedded representations. Using a method that combines natural language inference and knowledge projection, we establish significant structural similarities between the two vocabularies, particularly in their similarity matrices which show an 85% overlap. Our evaluation methods, including classification performance and human judgment, further validate the substantial equivalence of these two financial emotion lexicons, providing a foundation for effective use of the UNLEx dataset.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and resolved for fair-throughput optimisation is fair-throughput optimisation is addressed, a closed-form optimal allocation of the energy signal and data subcarriers is achieved, a critical factor determining the application of either only the data subcarriers or both the energy and data subcarriers is identified, a novel OFDM fairness metric is introduced, and an optimal sum-throughput is achieved by deploying both the energy and data subcarriers, a novel OFDM fairness metric is introduced to determine whether to use only the data subcarriers or both the energy and data subcarriers, a novel OFDM fairness metric is introduced, and finally, the theoretical findings are verified via numerical examples.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including Stefan problems, dendrite growth, and Rayleigh--B\'enard instabilities, even in the presence of melting boundaries.

In multiagent learning settings beyond finding equilibria, learning rationalizable behavior is another significant goal. However, existing algorithms focus primarily on equilibria and do not prioritize rationalizability. This article presents a novel ALGo that guarantees the multiplication of agents' strategies' expected utilities is bounded by the product of their individual utilities plus an adjustable error margin. This approach is applicable to multiple games, including simultaneously played, repeated, and stochastic. The algorithm's performance outperforms the current state-of-the-art in finding rationalizable equilibria by a factor of two. Moreover, it offers comparable or superior performance to algorithms designed for finding average welfare, Pareto optimality, or social welfare. The algorithm's vast utility is demonstrated by its ability to find rationalizable equilibria in complex games, such as the triopoly supply game.

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible to Infective to Recovered model is conducted, where the model is based on an Erdős-Rényi random graph that changes dynamically as susceptible individuals connected to infected neighbors form new connections or sever existing ones. As the model is scaled to accommodate large populations, researchers obtained mathematical proofs for the speed of disease spread matching previous models and a set of precise conditions where there is no long-term presence of infection in the population. It is demonstrated that two main factors influence whether isolated or highly connected nodes are most effective in preventing the long-term presence of infection.

Integrating diverse datasets, stemming from data and theoretical sources, is a prerequisite for accurately fitting probability density functions. While aligning with data is straightforward, incorporating theories poses greater complexity, especially when combining multiple sources. In this context, discrepancies or mismatches must be reconciled, and various implementations of the same physics process may differ subtly. To effectively compare theories with data, a consistent renormalization and factorization scheme is essential. Although matching and merging techniques can be applied universally to specific processes, a pivotal advancement is required to automatically integrate key standard processes, complete with all higher-order corrections, across varying phase spaces and particle decay scenarios, all while maintaining consistency in factorization schemes. Without such a method, combining datasets is significantly constrained, necessitating separate fits for each dataset and complicating interpretations that depend on the relationship between different PDF scales or qQbar evolution. This work presents the PyPDF toolkit, an open-source pipeline segment engineered to fit standard processes to datasets, enabling more comprehensive and flexible global PDF fits.

To accelerate policy optimization in complex, dynamic systems with multiple influencing factors, reinforcement learning agents can effectively utilize previously collected historical data. Standard experience replay enables agents to retain information from prior iterations. However, the current approach equally values all observations, neglecting their varying significance. A more advanced technique, variance reduction based experience replay, selectively leverages particular historical records that are less likely to change. The current method extends this concept by identifying informative records with substantial probabilities of remaining consistent. This extension can be applied to both policy optimization with proximal objective and stable off-policy evaluation. The proposed approach theoretically and empirically demonstrates superior performance compared to the conventional experience replay.

In our analysis of conversational dialogue, we face numerous possible responses 
to any given history, leading us to present the MultiTalk dataset. This large 
and diverse dataset comprises over 250,000 written conversational pairs between 
three individuals, expanding upon previous single-person conversational datasets. 
To accelerate real-world applications of dialogue generation models, we propose 
the use of massively diverse "branching" conversations rather than simply adding 
historical nodes. Our study includes three fundamental evaluation tasks 
assessed via the "bridge-game" concept. These tasks consist of producing the 
next statement in a conversation, summarizing an entire conversation, and 
creating a new, unconnected conversation. Our findings highlight the necessity 
for models capable of anticipating multiple potential conversation paths.

We introduce MG-GLAM, a computational tool developed to rapidly create comprehensive N-body simulations for various cosmological theories, specifically modified gravity models. This program builds upon the existing GLAM code and incorporates an advanced multigrid method to solve the non-linear equations characteristic of modified gravity theories, resulting in highly efficient simulations. For $f(R)$ gravity, MG-GLAM includes multiple variations that mimic distinct behaviors of these models and offers tailored algorithms to maintain speed and precision. The code excels at producing a broad spectrum of modified gravity simulations and offers significant computational benefits, outperforming existing N-body simulations by a factor of over a hundred while yielding accurate results for key cosmological metrics. MG-GLAM is suited for creating large sets of modified gravity simulations that can be utilized in mock galaxy catalogues and emulators for ongoing and future galaxy surveys.

Miller and Sheffield introduced the concept of an imaginary surface as a pairing of subdomains of the complex plane and associated Gaussian free fields under conformal equivalence. Specifically, they considered the relationship between these pairings and chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution. This paper develops Gaussian free field-valued processes in the upper half-plane and the first orthant of the complex plane, establishing their connection to multiple SLE evolving in time on these domains. We demonstrate that such connections can be made locally by driving multiple SLE with the Dyson model on the real line and the Bru-Wishart process on the positive reals, respectively. Ultimately, these pairings yield domains that evolve in time and associated Gaussian free fields.

MediaWiki's 'WorkingWiki' is an open-source extension that transforms a wiki
into a sophisticated collaborative platform for developing complex documents
and software projects.
It achieves this by integrating with development version control systems like
Git, enabling users to track changes, collaborate effectively, and maintain
a clear history of their work.
This paper describes the features of WorkingWiki, while demonstrating its
capabilities with cases that involve creating a complex, step-by-step
procedure and developing an open-source package in R.

This study undertakes a linear analysis of a methane-air jet flame experiencing turbulence to determine its response to acoustic vibrations emitted from upstream, while factoring in temperature fluctuations that can cause instability in flames. To accurately predict flame behavior in a linearized model, it is crucial to account for heat released from combustion, as well as mass and enthalpy reactions specific to methane. To apply this model, the researchers performed a detailed linearization of the flow around the flames during both transient starting phases and steady states. To validate their model, the team conducted experimental measurements of temperature, pressure, and flow velocity fluctuations at various distances from the source of vibrations for different frequencies, velocities, and atmospheric pressures. The team also developed an "active flame" method to capture non-linear interactions between the atmosphere and acoustic waves. The team found that the linear model accurately captured the behavior of temperature fluctuations and that the "active flame" approach effectively predicted velocity field fluctuations. The team discovered that mass and enthalpy reactions significantly influenced acoustic behavior and that the atmosphere could amplify or diminish oscillations. The researchers also observed that the direction of the jet flame affected the interaction with the atmosphere and that the atmosphere could significantly impact the distribution of temperature fluctuations in the jet. The team's study provides a comprehensive understanding of the interaction between the atmosphere and acoustic vibrations in jet flames.

We investigate the neutrinoless double beta decay driven by an extremely light dark matter field interacting with neutrinos, particularly focusing on the impact when the DM frequency matches the neutrino mass scale. The time-dependent nature of this interaction results in a neutrinoless double beta decay rate that relies on a specific combination of the neutrino mass matrix and the dark matter phase, which we find can either boost or hinder the decay rate by many orders of magnitude. The time-varying density of neutrinos produced by this interaction also influences the cosmological neutrino relic density and impact on the cosmic microwave background. However, the brief duration of the dark matter's oscillation in comparison to the expansion of the universe prevents further developments on the neutrino mass. Consequently, constraints from the neutrinoless double beta decay and cosmology are found to be comparable. We also note the possibility of observing an interference term in the cosmic neutrino background as the universe cools and the dark matter's oscillation period lengthens, which we find can be detected in future experiments for certain parameters.

Nonlocal gravity theory is a classical generalization of Einstein's gravity theory. Based on an analogy with nonlocal electrodynamics, this new model involves a history-dependent relation that can be confirmed through data. The purpose of this paper is to modify nonlocal gravity theory so that the nonlocal aspect relates directly to observable properties, similar to the approach in nonlocal electrodynamics. The reformulated theory results in a constitutive relation identical to one proposed recently by Puetzfeld, Obukhov, and Hehl. The nonlocal gravity theory can be applied to show that de Sitter spacetime does not meet the theory's requirements.

Understanding how genomic elements affect specific traits through genome-wide association studies remains complex due to the sheer number of available annotations. We've developed a statistical approach to pinpoint relevant genomic elements, based on associations across the entire genome, by identifying patterns of influence in trait-associated SNPs. This approach can incorporate multiple annotation types and has been successfully applied to eighteen human traits such as blood pressure, body mass index, and various cancer types, using data from the 1000 Genomes Project across the autosomes. Our results show that different traits affect genes in distinct ways, with traits varying in their association with enhancer regions, and that associations differ between coding and non-coding parts of the genome. Furthermore, we discovered that traits are more likely to influence genes that are functionally related, and that associations vary between chromosomes X and Y. A this approach can help us better understand the connection between the genome and specific traits and diseases in humans.

This paper discusses recent findings from the LHC involving small systems studied
by the ALICE, ATLAS and CMS collaborations. Due to the growing significance
of QCD in small systems, particularly in situations with high multiplicity, not
all pertinent research can be covered within this report. It primarily examines
measurements focusing on collective behavior in small systems and new results on
strangeness enhancement observed in proton-proton interactions. It is essential to
note that many notable findings have been excluded from the discussion presented
here.

Observations of some variable X-ray sources within the Milky Way's center that show little to no activity could potentially be linked to neutron stars in close orbits with their companion stars. The recurrence times of transients in the Milky Way's center provide support for this theory, as they align with the expected durations of an accretion bursts from an isolated neutron star. The recent discovery of an Isolated Neutron Star in the Milky Way's center strengthens this hypothesis. The nature of these quiescent sources remains unclear, with one possibility being low-mass X-ray binaries where the mass transfer has temporarily ceased. Based on the recurrence times of transients, we predict future outbursts and future discoveries of quiescent Isolated Neutron Stars in the Milky Way's center.

THz radiation enables the precise stimulation of vibrational frequencies in molecules and crystals, leading to the introduction of inertial influences on electrons. By drawing a comparison to classical mechanics, where circular motion generates Coriolis and centrifugal forces, analogous effects arise, specifically spin-rotation coupling, centrifugal field coupling, and the interplay of these forces with the spin-orbit and the redshift of energy levels. These effects can persist for a few picoseconds following the initial stimulation, and potentially amplifying their magnitude could make this approach a promising means of controlling localized quantum states and chemical reaction barriers via vibration.

Improving neural conversational agents' ability to produce diverse, engaging responses in casual conversations is a challenge. To tackle this issue, we introduced a new metric, semantic diversity, measured by adapting the Natural Language Inference framework. We also modified the standard training and generation methods of the seq2seq model to enhance its capacity for casual conversation. Experiments showed that our enhanced model not meets the basic requirements of a conversational model, but also scores significantly better on a diverse-generation assessment.

The occurrence of sustainable hydrogen burning in very low-mass stars might be impacted by rotation due to the addition of centrifugal force and potential break-up caused by rapid spinning. Computer simulations model rotating low-mass stars with the capability for sustained nuclear reactions, considering a range of rotation rates, rather than slow rotation alone. Using these simulations, we determined the boundaries within which stars could maintain nuclear energy through hydrogen burning. These boundaries varied based on angular momentum. However, above a certain threshold (approximately 8.85 x 10^48 erg s) the boundaries broke into two distinct branches, resulting from objects losing mass and experiencing extreme spin. This research was applied to model the development of sub-stellar objects. Two possible scenarios were modeled: one where objects maintain a constant level of spin as they grow, and another where they retain a constant amount of angular momentum. In both cases, the models indicated that the objects would shed mass and become highly rotated as they lost envelope material. These models also suggested that even tiny stars with the capability for sustained nuclear burning could be shed into the sea of gas around forming planetary systems.

The technique of amplitude analysis in hadron decay studies is quite effective, 
However, this analysis faces a major challenge in addressing instrumental influences 
such as fluctuations in background levels and selection efficiency across different 
multidimensional kinematic scenarios.  This article will review traditional methods 
used for calculating efficiency and background probability and discuss the application 
of two techniques specifically density estimation using Gaussian processes and 
artificial neural networks. The first approach demonstrates the application of 
parametric and non-parametric models using the decay of $D^0$ mesons to $K^- \bar{K}^0$, 
whereas the second highlights a comparison between different density estimation 
methods using the $D^0$ meson pair decay into $K_S^0 K^- \pi^+ \pi^+$.

A new model based on a comprehensive expression for radiation energy has been proposed, and it effectively elucidates the dynamics of afterglows in multiple contexts, including relativistic, non-relativistic phases and fireball radiations with radiative and adiabatic components.

Bipartite graphs depicting connections between distinct groups of objects have numerous practical applications, and their visualization often takes the form of a 2-tier layout where corresponding entities are aligned horizontally across two parallel lines, connected by lines representing relationships between them. The task of reducing edge crossings within these visualizations can be computationally intensive, yet might not always guarantee sufficiently low crossings levels to maintain the visualization's clarity. In contrast, an approach has been developed to remove edge crossings by splitting specific nodes, targeting the minimum number required to yield an edge-free (planar) drawing. The question of determining if an edge-free representation exists after breaking at most a specified number of nodes remains tractable in relation to that number.

This paper will present our progress in developing an advanced, bipedal robot that utilizes thrusters for increased efficiency and stability during challenging tasks. We will showcase several demonstrations of the robot successfully completing difficult maneuvers like swinging a baseball bat and jumping over obstacles without the thrusters, highlighting how they can be utilized to complete such actions. To show the thrusters' effectiveness, we will also present data comparing their use with and without, in relation to specific performance metrics. To achieve these results, we will discuss the control and modeling techniques that allowed the robot to execute these tasks smoothly.

Becker-Denef-Lipschitz first observed in 1979 that over finite fields $k$, the total residue map $\text{res}$ from Laurent series to $k$ is expressible in a specific language, provided $t$ is included as a parameter. This discovery motivated further research into the properties of a specific mathematical theory related to valued fields. In the course of these investigations, the authors proved that this theory does not have a certain desirable feature and demonstrated that, for infinite fields $k$, the associated power series fields cannot be computationally decided. This, in turn, led to an analogous undecidability conclusion for a specific complex-valued field of power series.

In order to enhance side-channel attacks, this research introduces a new technique, HyperDegrade, which incorporates previous methods and employs simultaneous multithreading architectures.  A novel analysis into the causes of performance degradation through cache eviction was also performed, leading to the discovery of an unknown source of slowdowns.  Compared to existing techniques, HyperDegrade results in more significant slowdowns and increases attack feasibility while decreasing the risk of detection.  Furthermore, HyperDegrade is applicable to a wide range of processors with simultaneous multithreading architectures and is relatively easy to implement, often requiring the addition of just a few lines of code or a single hardware component.

A localized alteration in knot diagrams is referred to as an unknotting operation. It can be demonstrated that any knot diagram can be transformed into a trivial unknot through a sequence of unknotting operations specific to the type of knot, whether classical or welded. This research result is comparable to a previous study by K. Ko (arXiv:1501.00544) which identified 21 distinct procedures that specifically target the welded fundamental group of the resulting unknot. We focus on one particular procedure, known as the "flip" operation applied to a whorl or cusp, and show that any knot, specifically the figure-eight knot, can be converted into the trivial unknot through a series of flip operations. Additionally, we provide a series examples that illustrate the resulting unknot can be achieved by applying other types of unknotting operations.

We've demonstrated that combining the 1-cocycle of a long knot's space with Fox-Hatcher 1-cycles through integration produces a specific Vassiliev invariant, having a precise order of three. This discovery builds on a prior finding by the second author, where in a different case, integrating these 1-cocycles yielded a Vassiliev invariant of the second order.

In cooperative systems with multiple agents, coordination enables tasks to be performed that would be beyond the capabilities of any single agent. We investigate the concept of coordination through strategic decision-making, focusing on a scenario where agents select between two tasks of varying difficulty that are randomly distributed and partially known. It has been found that a stable state of cooperation, characterized by a straightforward linear pattern, can be achieved when there is a wide range of possible task difficulties. Furthermore, it was discovered that the most advantageous strategy for the system to reach is often when robots voluntarily isolate themselves to work on isolated projects.
